title: Yellow Heart Emoji 💛 Meaning in Texts and on Snapchat
description: 💛 means friendship, happiness and platonic love. Here is what the yellow heart means on Snapchat, from a guy or a girl, and when it is not just friendly.
summary: The 💛 yellow heart emoji means friendship and cheerful, platonic love. It is the heart people send to best friends, family and anyone they want to encourage without romantic overtones. On Snapchat it has a fixed meaning: you and that person are each other's number one best friend.
meaning: Yellow is the color of sunshine and smiley faces, and this heart borrows that mood. It says “you make me happy” more than “I'm in love with you.” People attach it to good-morning texts, congratulations and thank-yous, and it is the usual choice when someone wants to show love to a friend of the gender they date without creating confusion.

Because friendship is its core, 💛 is the least ambiguous of the colored hearts. It rarely gets mistaken for a come-on. That is useful, and occasionally disappointing: a person hoping for romance who receives a steady stream of yellow hearts may reasonably conclude they are valued as a friend. Still, plenty of couples use it as “their” heart, and a sunny personality will send it to everyone.

It has a second, gentler job in hard moments. Yellow reads as hope, so 💛 is common in messages of support for someone who is ill, anxious or grieving, where red might feel too heavy and black too bleak. It is also widely used alongside yellow ribbons and in awareness campaigns that have adopted the color.

Then there is plain color-matching. Sunflowers, lemons, bees, autumn light, rubber ducks, a yellow dress or a team that plays in yellow all attract the emoji. Paired with 💙 it gives the colors of the Ukrainian flag; with 💚 it suits Brazil or Australia. Meaning in those cases comes from the pairing.

contexts.label: On Snapchat
contexts.body: A 💛 next to a friend's name is assigned by Snapchat, not sent by anyone. It means you send the most snaps to that person and they send the most to you. Keep that up for two weeks and it turns into a red heart ❤️; after two months it becomes 💕. Lose the top spot and the heart disappears.

contexts.label: Between friends
contexts.body: This is the default best-friend heart. It goes under graduation photos, in birthday posts and at the end of “love you, text me when you land.” It is especially handy in mixed-gender friendships, where it keeps affection clearly platonic. Many friend pairs treat it as a small tradition.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Mixed news, usually. A yellow heart shows the person likes you and feels comfortable, but it is not the color most people pick when they want to flirt. If their messages are otherwise full of compliments and plans to meet, ignore the color. If the yellow heart is the warmest thing you ever get, they may see you as a friend.

contexts.label: In support messages
contexts.body: For someone having a rough week, 💛 offers brightness without pressure. “Thinking of you 💛” and “one day at a time 💛” are typical. It is a kind option when you want to send strength to an acquaintance or colleague and a red heart would feel too intimate.

examples.text: Happy birthday to my day one 💛
examples.meaning: Deep friendship; the sender is celebrating a longtime best friend.
Platonic joy at someone else's good news.

examples.text: Hope today is kinder to you 💛
examples.meaning: Gentle encouragement during a difficult time.
A caption matching the yellow theme of the photo.

examples.meaning: They noticed Snapchat marks them as mutual number one best friends.
A warm compliment about someone's cheerful personality.

combos.meaning: Sunny, happy affection, or a caption for sunflower and summer photos.
The colors of the Ukrainian flag, used to show support for Ukraine.
Golden, glowing positivity; often used for good news or a lovely memory.
Bee-themed cuteness, as in “bee happy,” or the colors of a yellow-and-black team.

confusedWith.difference: 🧡 is a shade warmer and has a seasonal tie to autumn. Both are friendly, but orange is the one linked to the friend-zone joke, while yellow has the established best-friend meaning, helped by Snapchat.
💖 is pink with glittering stars and expresses excited, sweet affection that can easily be romantic. 💛 is flatter in tone and firmly platonic unless the people involved have decided otherwise.
❤️ is love at full strength and the romantic default. 💛 is love as friendship and good cheer. On Snapchat the difference is literal: yellow comes first and red replaces it after two weeks.

avoid: If you are trying to show romantic interest, do not lead with it; most people read yellow as friendship.
Avoid it in messages about very fresh grief unless you know the person welcomes brightness.
Do not read too much into the Snapchat version, which reflects snap counts and can change within days.
design: A solid heart in bright yellow, drawn in the same shape as each platform's red heart. Apple and Samsung give it a golden, slightly glossy finish, and flatter designs elsewhere use a pure lemon yellow. It was one of four colored hearts in the original 2010 emoji set, with green, blue and purple, so it displays reliably on practically every device.

faqs.q: What does 💛 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Most likely that she values you as a friend or is simply in a happy mood. Girls commonly use it with their closest friends. If she is your girlfriend and yellow is her favorite color, it is just her style of heart and no cause for concern.

faqs.q: What does 💛 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Often that he wants to be warm without sounding romantic. It is a comfortable heart for men to send friends and relatives. If he is flirting in his words while using yellow, trust the words.

faqs.q: How do I get the yellow heart on Snapchat?
faqs.a: You and one friend have to be each other's top contact, meaning you each send more snaps to the other than to anyone else. The app adds the heart automatically once that is true and removes it when it stops being true.

faqs.q: Is the yellow heart ever romantic?
faqs.a: Occasionally. Some couples adopt it, and a person who loves the color may use it for everyone, partner included. As a general signal, though, it sits at the friendly end of the heart spectrum.

faqs.q: Does the yellow heart mean jealousy or cowardice?
faqs.a: No. Although yellow has those associations in some old sayings, the emoji is not used that way. In practice it is consistently positive: friendship, happiness, hope and support.
